scope: authentication of an external WebAuthn verifier result and its build identity

result_authentication_options.mechanism: execute an allowlisted verifier binary locally and consume its result over a private process boundary
strengths: result can be bound directly to caller nonce and exact input digests
residual_risks: compromised host can replace the process or forge IPC
binary digest alone does not prove source, configuration or execution integrity

result_authentication_options.mechanism: DSSE-sign the closed result with a dedicated offline-verifiable verifier-result key
strengths: explicit payload type and exact-byte signature binding
residual_risks: key compromise can mint convincing results
signature proves key use but not which binary executed
requires independent root, epoch, revocation and replay policy

result_authentication_options.mechanism: hardware-backed workload quote binds nonce, result digest and measured verifier identity
strengths: can bind execution measurement to freshness
reduces reliance on an exportable result-signing key
residual_risks: vendor endorsement and revocation roots become trust dependencies
measurement may omit runtime configuration or mutable dependencies
large parser, privacy and cross-platform policy surface

result_authentication_options.mechanism: bind the result to an OIDC identity, short-lived certificate and transparency proof
residual_risks: OIDC, CA, transparency log and inclusion policy add shared control planes
offline acceptance needs pinned roots and checkpoint freshness

build_identity_sources.claim: two independent builders reproduce the exact verifier artifact digest from pinned source and dependencies
signed provenance binds source, builder, parameters, dependencies and artifact digest
a platform quote reports an allowlisted executable or workload measurement
does_not_prove: complete mutable state unless explicitly measured

build_identity_sources.claim: distribution metadata names exact package or image bytes

selection_prerequisites: single-use caller nonce and evidence ledger
signed provenance checked separately from byte equality
negative corpus and parser differential tests
explicit platform configuration and dependency measurement policy
documented key or workload identity rotation and incident recovery
